bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / sample_info.json / exact staged vulnerable source / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` in `_mum_hash_aligned` with project frames `ucl_hash_func -> ucl_hash_search -> ucl_object_insert_key_common`, and the allocation stack points back to `ucl_object_copy_internal` inside `.inherit`. In the exact staged vulnerable source, a JSON-style quoted key is copied through `ucl_copy_or_store_ptr()` and unescaped by `ucl_unescape_json_string()`, so a `\u0000` escape in the attacker input becomes a literal embedded NUL byte inside the owned key buffer while the returned decoded `keylen` still counts bytes after that NUL. `ucl_parse_key()` stores that pointer-length pair in a `ucl_object_t`, and the object is retained in the parser's object graph. Later the same input executes the `.inherit` context macro; `ucl_inherit_handler()` resolves the named parent object, iterates one of its children with that embedded-NUL key, and copies it with `ucl_object_copy_internal()`. The copy path first `memcpy()`s the whole source object, preserving the full `keylen`, then deep-copies `other->trash_stack[UCL_TRASH_KEY]` with `strdup()`, which truncates the new backing allocation at the first embedded NUL. Because `new->keylen` was already preserved from the source object, the copied object now carries a short `new->key` allocation but the original full logical length. Re-inserting that copy into the target object hashes `copy->key` for `copy->keylen` bytes, and `_mum_hash_aligned()` over-reads 8 bytes past the `strdup` allocation. The saved patch fixes exactly this mismatch by replacing `strdup` with a length-based allocation and `memcpy(other->keylen)`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled malformed key state. On the vulnerable path, this in-place JSON unescape decodes a quoted key containing `\u0000` into an owned key buffer that now contains a literal embedded NUL while `ret` remains the full decoded key length.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness `gt_results/arvo_38675/poc` is 819 bytes (sha256 `37feb50b77667e329d3e137712ee4aea772efd73004fdfa737ea6ea1c1a22cdd`). Static byte inspection shows a literal `\u0000` sequence at offset 160 and multiple `.inherit` directives beginning at offsets 488, 530, 595, 660, 702, and 744. This source step is reached only after `ucl_parse_key()` accepts a JSON-style quoted key and `ucl_lex_json_string()` sets `need_unescape = true` for that key body.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The low-level hasher reads an 8-byte word from `str` while hashing the copied key for `len == copy->keylen`; because the copied key storage was truncated by `strdup` at the first embedded NUL, this read crosses the right edge of that heap allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 8` at `src/./mum.h:230:32`, 0 bytes to the left of the allocation end at `0x60c0000002fa`, with crash stack `_mum_hash_aligned -> _mum_hash_default -> mum_hash -> ucl_hash_func`.

root_cause.description: The copy path duplicates an embedded-NUL key with `strdup`, which allocates only through the first NUL. Because the earlier whole-object `memcpy()` has already preserved the source `keylen`, rebinding `new->key` to this short allocation creates a pointer-length mismatch later consumed by hashing.
root_cause.note: The patch replaces this with `malloc(other->keylen)` plus `memcpy(..., other->keylen)`, confirming that the missing obligation is to copy key storage by explicit `keylen`, not C-string termination.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete attacker-derived byte origin. When the parsed escape is `\u0000`, this statement writes a literal `0x00` byte into the owned key buffer instead of treating it as the end of the logical key.
tainted_value_origin.note: The function later returns `t - str` at line 431, so bytes copied after this embedded NUL remain part of the logical decoded key length that propagates into `keylen`.

parser_admitted.description: The key parser admits the witness into JSON-style quoted-key handling instead of the bare-identifier path. That quoted-key path is what allows `ucl_lex_json_string()` to flag escapes and `ucl_copy_or_store_ptr()` to take the unescape call at the scored source.

fine_trace.note: Source. `ucl_parse_key()` has already routed a JSON-style quoted key into `ucl_copy_or_store_ptr()` with `need_unescape = true`. This call decodes the copied key text in place; for the staged witness, a `\u0000` escape becomes a literal embedded `0x00` byte inside `*dst`, but `ret` remains the full decoded key length, including bytes after that NUL.

The parser stores the decoded key buffer and returned logical length into the new object. On the vulnerable path the key buffer now contains an embedded NUL from step 1 but `keylen` still counts the trailing bytes, so `nobj->keylen > strlen(nobj->key)`.

The object carrying the embedded-NUL key is retained in the parser's current object graph. That preserved `nobj->key` / `nobj->keylen` pair is what later becomes one of the `parent` children iterated by `.inherit`.

Later in the same input, the `.inherit` context macro resolves a parent object by attacker-controlled name inside `ctx == parser->top_obj`. The vulnerable copy path continues only because this lookup returns a real object instead of taking the early error return.

The handler iterates the inherited parent's children until it reaches one whose key is the embedded-NUL key preserved in steps 2-3. For that child, the duplicate check does not `continue`, so control enters `ucl_object_copy(cur)` and the later re-insertion path becomes reachable.
The whole-object copy clones the source object's metadata before deep-copying the key storage, so `new->keylen` is preserved as the original full decoded key length from steps 2-5.

Root cause. `strdup()` stops at the first embedded NUL, so the new backing allocation only holds the key prefix through that NUL. Because step 6 has already preserved the source `new->keylen`, rebinding `new->key` here creates a copied object whose pointer refers to a short C-string allocation but whose logical key length still spans bytes after the NUL.

The inherited copy is reinserted into the target object. This search object now carries the truncated `copy->key` pointer from step 7 together with the stale full `copy->keylen`, so the hash lookup is asked to examine more bytes than the copied key allocation contains.
The hash layer forwards the copied key pointer and the full logical key length directly into the MUM hasher. No check re-derives the usable length from the truncated allocation or from `strlen`.

Sink. `_mum_hash_aligned()` reads 8-byte words from `str` while hashing `len == copy->keylen` bytes. Because the actual allocation from step 7 ends at the embedded NUL, this word read crosses the heap boundary and matches the saved ASan `READ of size 8` at `src/./mum.h:230`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix replaces `strdup(other->trash_stack[UCL_TRASH_KEY])` with a length-based allocation and `memcpy(..., other->keylen)` before rebinding `new->key`, so the copied key storage matches the logical `keylen` even when the key contains embedded NUL bytes.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged vulnerable source, staged patch.diff, and static byte inspection of gt_results/arvo_38675/poc

format.name: UCL parser input with embedded-NUL inherited key
format.contract: Exact staged 819-byte witness (sha256 `37feb50b77667e329d3e137712ee4aea772efd73004fdfa737ea6ea1c1a22cdd`). Static inspection shows a literal `\u0000` escape at byte offset 160 and later `.inherit` directives at offsets 488, 530, 595, 660, 702, and 744. On the reproduced path, at least one JSON-style quoted key is unescaped so the owned key buffer contains an embedded NUL while `keylen` still covers later bytes, and a later `.inherit` copy reuses that key through `ucl_object_copy_internal()` before the copied child is reinserted and hashed.
